the evaluation of the role of soluble adhesion molecule and chemokine levels in serum and ascites in SBP.
the study of the inflammatory process in patients with SBPs.

the evaluation of serum or ascitic fluid levels in SBP patients is not useful.

serum and ascitic levels of chemokine and adhesion molecules could be implicated in peritoneal inflammation in cirrhotic ascites, and that the evaluation of serum levels of IC‐AM‐1 and VCA‐M‐1 could be useful to identify high‐risk patients with SBP.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the serum and ascitic levels of chemokine and adhesion molecules may have prognostic and diagnostic implications in SBP.
the levels of soluble adhesions molecules and chemokine levels in ascitic fluid and serum may have a prognostic role and could be used as a marker of the inflammatory response in patients with SBPs.
the serum and ascitic levels of soluble adhesions molecules and cytokines are increased in patients with SBPs, but their role in the pathogenesis of this condition is not completely understood.

the evaluation of the levels of adhesion and chemokine molecules in the serum and ascitic fluids of patients with SBP could be useful to better understand their pathophysiology and to predict their clinical course and outcome.
